chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya who said: Abu Qurra the Hadith scholar asked me to facilitate his entrance into the presence of Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him) … so Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

If the narrations contradict the Qur’an then I reject them, and what the Muslims have all unanimously agreed upon is that He cannot be fully comprehended by knowledge, and the eye-sight cannot overtake Him, and there is nothing like Him.
ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars determine if a hadith is authentic based on the Qur'an?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the criterion for accepting or rejecting hadith narrations by comparing them to the Qur’an. He further elaborates on the divine attribute of incomprehensibility, citing the consensus of Muslims that God's essence is beyond full human knowledge and sight, and that there is nothing comparable to Him.
